items.title: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes
items.summary: City-scale 3D grounding is commonly formulated as candidate ranking, which requires precomputed instance proposals and becomes inefficient in large outdoor scenes. We propose Urbex, an agentic vision-language framework that instead casts grounding as active spatial search. items.title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
items.summary: Large language models have evolved from single-turn chatbots into interactive agents capable of long-horizon reasoning. In real deployments, MCP tool services can return noisy feedback and users may intervene to correct the agent, but existing methods provide limited supervision for reflection learning and failure recovery. To bridge this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflection in agents.

items.summary: System one models enable direct, low-latency decision-making. items.summary: Determining whether an image is AI-generated does not establish whether the situation it depicts is factually supported. items.summary: Generating information-rich visual artifacts such as slides, posters, and dashboards as code is appealing because the outputs are structured, editable, and verifiable. items.summary: Finding the right video often requires distinguishing similar scenes in which different events occur. items.summary: Large language model agents are emerging as an important new class of users of desktop applications. items.title: ReTerm: Recovery Training for Self-Improving Terminal Agents
items.summary: Terminal agents have shown strong abilities in complex coding tasks. However, they often struggle to recover from errors during long-running execution (e.g., command errors, faulty implementations), eventually leading to task failures. items.title: GeoFix: Geometry Fixing for 4D Consistent Generation
items.summary: Video diffusion models increasingly serve as priors for 4D generation, but the generated videos often lack geometric consistency. Recent approaches address this through post-training by designing geometric rewards, yet this can degrade texture and fine detail, requiring auxiliary appearance rewards and careful reward balancing. To address this challenge, we propose GeoFix, a unified framework that improves geometric consistency and visual quality
